title: Transformers: Yet Another Data Center Power Infrastructure Supply Chain Bottleneck
key_facts: The article is produced in collaboration between Maddox Industrial Transformer and Bisnow's Studio B; Bisnow news staff were not involved.
Jordan Castaneda, data center sales manager at Maddox, says the 'real bottleneck' for data centre developers is now power, not capital or land.
Transformers step voltage up or down to usable levels for data centres; Castaneda says procurement is a critical speed-to-market issue.
Castaneda cites the Department of Energy as expecting data centres to take 12% of US electricity by 2028.
Maddox, based in Washington state, presents itself as a third option between slow big manufacturers and cheaper imports, holding thousands of transformers in stock.
The article is promotional for Maddox.
quote_evidence: This article was produced in collaboration between Maddox Industrial Transformer and Studio B. Bisnow news staff was not involved in the production of this content.
For data center developers, securing capital and land is no longer the chief bottleneck to getting projects built.
why_it_matters_hint: Power equipment supply is described as a constraint on data centre building, by a company that sells it.
